s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopy showing segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopy showing segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, and colonoscopy findings of segmental erythema and ulceration are consistent with ulcerative colitis

shortlist.label: Crohn's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms to ulcerative colitis, and biopsy findings of subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate could be seen in Crohn's disease

shortlist.label: Infectious Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Despite negative stool cultures, infectious colitis remains a possibility given the acute onset of symptoms and evidence of colonic inflammation

shortlist.label: Microscopic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated fecal calprotectin and normal colonoscopy appearance in some areas suggest microscopic colitis as a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ischemic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea could be indicative of ischemic colitis, although the lack of significant risk factors and normal blood pressure make it less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea, along with the elevated C-reactive protein and fecal calprotectin, suggest an inflammatory process. The absence of significant past medical history, normal complete blood count, and negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays, combined with the acute onset and segmental nature of the colonoscopy findings, point towards an infectious cause rather than a chronic inflammatory bowel disease like Ulcerative Colitis or Crohn's Disease.

rejected.label: Ulcerative Colitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more chronic course and diffuse inflammation rather than segmental erythema and ulceration

rejected.label: Crohn's Disease
rejected.why: Often involves the entire thickness of the bowel wall and can have granulomas on biopsy, which were not found in this case

rejected.label: Microscopic Colitis
rejected.why: Characterized by normal endoscopic appearance with inflammation only visible on histology, which does not match the segmental erythema and ulceration seen on colonoscopy

rejected.label: Ischemic Colitis
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older patients with risk factors for vascular disease, and the biopsy would more likely show ischemic changes rather than an acute inflammatory infiltrate
